hook: There's a technique called thought scheduling. You don't clear your mind. You give the rumination a time slot — and your brain learns to wait.
topic: Worry postponement / thought scheduling — the clinical technique with strong trial support
body:
**Thought scheduling sounds strange until you try it. Then it sounds obvious.**

Here's how it works. You choose a specific time each day — let's say 5pm, fifteen minutes. That is your designated worry window. Every time a ruminating thought appears during the day, instead of engaging with it or suppressing it, you do one thing: you acknowledge it and postpone it. "I hear you. We'll deal with this at five."
